examples.title: IEEE 14-bus, with machines and controls
examples.summary: The IEEE 14-bus system with a round-rotor machine, an exciter and a governor on each generator: the usual first case for a power flow, a fault study and the eigenvalue analysis.

citations.text: IEEE 14 Bus Test Case, Power Systems Test Case Archive, University of Washington, Department of Electrical Engineering, https://labs.ece.uw.edu/pstca/pf14/pg_tca14bus.htm (accessed 2026-11-17).

H. Cui, F. Li and K. Tomsovic, "Hybrid Symbolic-Numeric Framework for Power System Modeling and Analysis," IEEE Transactions on Power Systems, vol. 36, no. 2, pp. 1373-1384, March 2021, doi:10.1109/TPWRS.2020.3017019.

licence.attribution: ANDES asks that research or consulting that uses it cite its paper, which is among the citations of this case (ANDES README, section Citing ANDES).

The power flow data is a PSS/E version prepared by J. Conto and distributed with ANDES. It has not been compared with the data of the University of Washington archive.

examples.title: Kundur two-area system, modified by ANDES
examples.summary: Four generators in two areas joined by a weak tie, the standard case for inter-area oscillations, with a round-rotor machine, an exciter and a governor on each generator.

citations.text: P. Kundur, Power System Stability and Control. New York: McGraw-Hill, 1994, ISBN 0-07-035958-X.
M. Klein, G. J. Rogers and P. Kundur, "A fundamental study of inter-area oscillations in power systems," IEEE Transactions on Power Systems, vol. 6, no. 3, pp. 914-921, 1991, doi:10.1109/59.119229.

caveats: This is not the system of the book as printed. The file's own title is "Modified Kundur's two-area test system, distributed with ANDES", and it has 10 buses where the book's system has 11. Do not compare its results with the book's without checking the data.
One event is built into the file: Line_8 is switched out at 2 s.

examples.title: WSCC 9-bus, network only
examples.summary: The WSCC 3-machine, 9-bus network with its loads and generator set-points, for power flow. The file has no machine models, so there is nothing to simulate in the time domain.

citations.text: P. M. Anderson and A. A. Fouad, Power System Control and Stability. IEEE Press, 2002, doi:10.1109/9780470545577.
